title: "quarto-index empty-level probe"
from: markdown-smart
filters:

# An empty level in the middle of an entry

`!` separates sub-entry levels, so a value that opens, closes, or consists of
one puts a level in the entry that prints no text at all. The LaTeX index tool
rejects an entry whose first or middle level is empty — "Illegal null field" —
drops it, and still exits cleanly, so the entry disappears from a build that
looks fine. An empty level therefore prints nothing and is dropped, in every
format, and the entry indexes at the levels that remain.

Only two shapes can be written. A run of `!` yields at most one separator,
because `!!` is a literal exclamation mark, so two separators can never sit
side by side and a level between two others can never be empty.

A leading empty level, the shape that destroys the entry:
[cats]{.index entry="!Cats"}.

A trailing empty level, which the index tool tolerates by swallowing it, so
the two shapes fail in opposite ways and neither is evidence about the other:
[dogs]{.index entry="Dogs!"}.

Two empty levels around one that survives, so a mark can be seen to warn once
per empty level rather than once per mark: [sub]{.index entry="!Sub!"}.

# An empty level next to the rest of the syntax

A cross-reference whose target is the entry's own surviving level. The target
already dropped its empty levels; now the entry does too, so the two spellings
meet and the self-reference is reported in every format:
[owls]{.index entry="!Owls" see="Owls"}.

A sort key written across both levels. The key at the empty level goes with it,
so the surviving level keeps the key written for it and files under `aardvark`
rather than under `mmm`: [zebra]{.index entry="!Zebra" sort="mmm!aardvark"}.

# An entry that is nothing but empty levels

Nothing survives the drop, so there is no entry to index and the mark says so
rather than claiming no `entry=` was written.

With visible text to fall back on, the mark indexes under that text:
[Ferrets]{.index entry="!"}.

With no visible text and nothing to fall back on, the mark indexes nothing and
is removed: []{.index entry="!"}.

# A control with no empty level

Two ordinary levels, so a check that the empty ones are gone is told apart from
a check that lost every level: [wrens]{.index entry="Birds!Wrens"}.
